bell-2.qiskit_code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector
import math

qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 2)   # 2 seeds, one classical bit each
qc.h(0)        # Split (Hadamard): one path becomes two equal paths
qc.cx(0, 1)    # Link (CNOT): the control seed decides whether the target flips
qc.measure([0, 1], [0, 1])   # Bloom: measure every seed

# Ideal probabilities, before any shots:
state = Statevector.from_instruction(qc.remove_final_measurements(inplace=False))
print(state.probabilities_dict())

# Run it. On Qollab `backend` is the device you picked; locally use AerSimulator().
job = backend.run(qc, shots=256)
print(job.result().get_counts())

from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector
import math

qc = QuantumCircuit(3, 3)   # 3 seeds, one classical bit each
qc.h(0)        # Split (Hadamard): one path becomes two equal paths
qc.p(-math.pi / 2, 0)   # Twist (phase gate): rotates the |1> path; invisible until paths recombine
